FIRST RUN — requirements §4
Google first, because it carries the calendar. The connect screen earns the permission by saying plainly what is read and what is never touched, then segments are chosen as a plain checklist rather than decorative tiles.

THE COMMAND CENTRE — requirements §5.1 to §5.3
Not a calendar. The dashboard opens with a written line, then Needs Attention, then the week, then a ledger of segments. Dates sit right-aligned in monospace so deadlines line up and can be scanned in one pass; red is reserved for things that are actually late.

ADDING, ASKING, CONTROLLING — requirements §5.4 to §5.8
One spoken sentence becomes two proposed items, each editable, neither saved until confirmed. Where the assistant is unsure it says so rather than presenting a guess as fact.
